description: Team Green is developing an interactive 3D visualization of how atmospheric carbon dioxide changes over time. Using NASA OCO-2 observations, we plan to compare the areas around Antalya and Istanbul and show the direction, rate, and uncertainty of each trend.
summary: InvisiTrace is an interactive browser tool for exploring atmospheric change around Antalya, Istanbul, New York, Tokyo, and London. It compares June 2019–2023 using four NASA satellite data products. Choose a city and variable to explore regional values on a rotatable globe, compare two years, and inspect an exploratory linear slope with a 95% confidence interval. The tool shows missing data and reports how many days contribute to each CO₂ value, helping learners understand how coverage affects a trend.
details:
To run the interactive demo, open the Project link, click Download in Google Drive, then open InvisiTrace_2026_EN.html in your web browser.

The app runs offline in a single HTML file using JavaScript and Canvas. A Python and NumPy workflow prepares 99 summaries from NASA NetCDF and HDF data. For CO₂, we average valid 1° grid values within 250 km of each city centre each day and give the available days equal weight. Water vapour and total column ozone use monthly 1° grids. Nitrous oxide uses the nearest Aura/MLS 4° × 5° grid point at 46.4 hPa. Near Antalya, available-day XCO₂ rose from 409.58 ppm in June 2019 to 418.06 ppm in June 2023. The fitted slope is +2.12 ppm/year (95% CI +1.36 to +2.88). Tokyo has no qualifying June 2019 value. Its 2020–2023 interval includes zero. The time series are short and sampling varies by city and year. The project builds on Team Green’s 2025 education concept with new data and comparisons. ChatGPT/Codex assisted with code, data extraction scripts, localization and presentation materials. Numeric data came from the cited NASA products.
